extracted.intended_audience: Obligated parties under the RFS program (refiners, blenders, fuel importers/exporters, renewable fuel producers including biogas/RNG producers), regulated industry counsel, EPA stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule amending 40 CFR part 80 to extend the 2024 Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) compliance reporting deadline and to make related clarifications, technical corrections, and an ASTM update. Targets how and when obligated parties must report and document compliance for the 2024 compliance year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of 2024 RFS compliance reporting deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is extending the 2024 RFS compliance reporting deadline from March 31, 2025, to the next quarterly compliance reporting deadline after the effective date of the final rule establishing the revised 2024 cellulosic biofuel standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: provide obligated parties additional time to carry out and adjust compliance strategies once the revised 2024 cellulosic biofuel standard is finalized and to avoid duplicative reporting. Example: if the final rule establishing the revised 2024 cellulosic biofuel standard is published May 15, 2025 (effective July 14, 2025), the 2024 compliance reporting deadline would be September 1, 2025. By operation of law the 2024 attest engagement deadline would also be extended (see attest engagement entry). EPA relied on APA section 553(d) exceptions and D.C. Circuit precedent to make the rule operational upon signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2024 annual compliance reports submission rule (§80.1451(f)(1)(i)(B)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 2024 compliance year, annual compliance reports must be submitted by the next quarterly reporting deadline under paragraph (f)(2) of this section after the date the revised 2024 cellulosic biofuel standard becomes effective in §80.1405(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the specific regulatory text implementing the extension described above. It ties the 2024 annual report submission date directly to the effective date of the revised 2024 cellulosic biofuel standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attest engagement deadline consolidation (§80.1464(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligated parties must submit annual attest engagement reports to EPA by the next June 1 annual attest engagement reporting deadline after the annual compliance reporting deadline under §80.1451(f)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA consolidated and simplified previously redundant, year‑specific attest engagement language. The simplified language does not change the deadline for any compliance year but clarifies that the attest engagement deadline is always the next June 1 after the compliance reporting deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly reporting deadlines schedule (40 CFR 80.1451(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The quarterly reporting deadlines are March 31, June 1, September 1, and December 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dates are the anchor points used to calculate the extended 2024 compliance reporting deadline and other timing obligations under the RFS annual reporting framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Batch number format for biogas producers (§80.105(j)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A biogas producer must assign a batch number to each batch of biogas consisting of their EPA-issued company registration number, the EPA-issued facility registration number, the last two digits of the compliance year in which the batch was produced, and a unique number for the batch beginning with the number one for the first batch produced each compliance year and each subsequent batch being assigned the next sequential number (e.g., 4321-54321-23-000001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that batch numbers are numbered based on the compliance year (not calendar year). The rule provides the exact composition and sequencing requirement and example formats to ensure consistent identification of batches for RIN generation and recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Batch number format for RNG producers and biogas closed distribution system RIN generators (§80.110(j)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The RNG producer, RNG importer, or biogas closed distribution system RIN generator must assign a batch number to each batch of RNG or biogas-derived renewable fuel consisting of their EPA-issued company registration number, the EPA-issued facility registration number, the last two digits of the compliance year in which the batch was produced, and a unique number for the batch beginning with the number one for the first batch produced each compliance year and each subsequent batch being assigned the next sequential number (e.g., 4321-54321-23-000001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel requirement to §80.105(j)(3) for RNG and RIN generators to ensure uniform batch numbering across fuel types subject to the RFS program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated biodiesel standard: incorporation of ASTM D6751-24
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is updating the reference in 40 CFR part 80 to ASTM D6751-24, Standard Specification for Biodiesel Fuel Blendstock (B100) for Middle Distillate Fuels, approved March 1, 2024, to define the quality of biodiesel that may participate in the RFS program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: industry updated the ASTM D6751 standard, and EPA updates the regulatory citation to be consistent with the most recent industry standard (many states use ASTM D6751-24). Copies may be obtained from ASTM International; the IBR is approved for §80.2. Stakeholders should use ASTM D6751-24 as the ASTM reference for biodiesel quality under the RFS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference list (§80.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text added/revised in §80.12 to incorporate by reference standards such as SM 2540, Solids (revised June 10, 2020; IBR approved for §80.155(c)) and ASTM D6751-24 (IBR approved for §80.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which external technical standards are incorporated into the regulation and the specific regulatory sections for which they apply. Gives procurement/source information for obtaining the standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition revisions in §80.2: 'Glycerin' and 'Locomotive engine'
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §80.2 by revising the definitions: 'Glycerin means a co-product from the production of biodiesel that primarily contains glycerol.' 'Locomotive engine means an engine used in a locomotive as defined under 40 CFR 1033.901.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definition changes correct a typo and replace a cross-reference; they clarify regulated terms used throughout Part 80 so obligated parties and enforcement personnel have precise definitional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart A / Subpart M amendment: blenders handling <250,000 gallons and tactical military vehicle exemption (§80.1440(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: §80.1440(f)(1) revised to list tactical military vehicles, engines, or equipment having an EPA national security exemption from emission standards under 40 CFR 85.1708, 1042.635, or 1068.225 as examples covered by the provision for blenders who handle and blend less than 250,000 gallons of renewable fuel per year or blend under a national security exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies categories of fuels/equipment that fall within the small‑volume blender provisions (exemptions) and the applicable CFR authorities for national security exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical corrections and clarifications to 40 CFR part 80 (Table II.C-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is making minor technical amendments to correct inaccuracies and clarify current regulations, including: correcting a typo in the definition of 'Glycerin'; replacing a cross-reference to a deleted provision in the definition of 'Locomotive engine'; clarifying that batch numbers are numbered based on the compliance year rather than the calendar year (§§80.105(j)(3) and 80.110(j)(3)); removing cross-references to deleted provisions (§80.1440(f)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are described in Table II.C-1 and are intended to remove ambiguities or outdated references. Stakeholders should treat these as clarifying, non-substantive changes to improve regulatory coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exporters' RVO timing and relationship to annual reporting (§80.1430(f) and note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exporters of renewable fuel are required to satisfy exporter RVOs within 30 days of exporting the renewable fuel under 40 CFR 80.1430(f). These exporter RVO retirements are not tied to the 2024 annual compliance reporting deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes that while exporters must submit annual compliance reports per §80.1451 (which summarize export activity), exporter RVO retirements occur on a 30-day schedule tied to the export event and are independent of the extended annual reporting deadline. The extension does not allow retroactive change to RIN retirement timing for exports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability guidance — who may be affected; determine applicability by 40 CFR part 80
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities potentially affected include those involved with production, distribution, and sale of transportation fuels (e.g., gasoline and diesel) and renewable fuels (e.g., ethanol, biodiesel, renewable diesel, and biogas). The preamble lists NAICS codes and examples but states the table is not exhaustive and directs readers to examine the applicability criteria in 40 CFR part 80 to determine whether the action applies to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure whether your entity is affected, carefully examine 40 CFR part 80 and consult the contact in the 'FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT' section. The listing of NAICS codes is illustrative only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date, operational date, and APA justification for immediate effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule is effective on March 13, 2025; for operational purposes under the CAA, the final rule is effective as of March 7, 2025. EPA states APA section 553(d) generally requires 30 days before effectiveness but the rule relieves a restriction and thus an exception applies; EPA also finds good cause under APA section 553(d)(3) given the need to avoid confusion if the extension did not take effect before the revised 2024 cellulosic biofuel standard was finalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble cites D.C. Circuit precedent and APA provisions providing the legal basis for making the rule operational upon signature. Obligated parties should use the effective/operational dates specified to determine when new deadlines and IBR approvals apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority and administrative findings (PRA, RFA, UMRA, EO analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory authority: sections 114, 203-05, 208, 211, and 301 of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7414, 7522-24, 7542, 7545, and 7601). Administrative findings: not a significant regulatory action under EO 12866; alleviates regulatory burden under EO 14192; does not impose new information collection burden under the PRA (OMB control numbers previously approved); certifies no significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the RFA; contains no unfunded mandates under UMRA; no federalism or tribal implications under EO 13132 and EO 13175; not subject to EO 13045 or EO 13211.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are EPA's legal and administrative determinations supporting promulgation and implementation of the rule and explain why certain review/analysis requirements do or do not apply. Useful for stakeholders assessing procedural posture and impact assessments of the rule.
